Both traces simulate the same 17-event FSM and arrive at identical results (READY, A=false, T=true, n=6, 5 rejections, first at index 5). Their approaches diverge in verification strategy. Trace 1 performs targeted step-by-step checks and explores one hypothetical—whether rejecting step 11 HELLO would change the outcome—concluding it would not. Trace 2 instead re-executes the full simulation twice from scratch. Both contain a full re-execution loop, but Trace 2 has two while Trace 1 has one. The hypothetical in Trace 1 is a grounded alternative that is explicitly explored and discarded, qualifying as a CYCLE.

⟦CYCLE⟧ trace=1 conf=probable start="What if Step 11 HELLO was rejected?" end="So yes, doesn't matter." basis=The solver opens a grounded alternative branch (HELLO rejected) and traces it through steps 12-15, explicitly concluding the final A value is unchanged.
⟦LOOP⟧ trace=1 conf=clear start="Let's re-verify the whole trace carefully." end="Everything consistent." basis=The solver re-executes all 17 steps in paraphrased form (using F/T shorthand), confirming the same states and rejections already computed in the main simulation.
⟦LOOP⟧ trace=2 conf=clear start="Initial: State=INIT, A=F, T=F, n=0" end="Correct, rejected." basis=The solver re-executes all 17 events from the beginning in a "Final Verification" block, reproducing the same state transitions and rejection decisions already established.
⟦LOOP⟧ trace=2 conf=clear start="Let's trace again just to be absolutely sure." end="Everything seems consistent." basis=A second full re-execution of all 17 steps, adding no new information beyond what the main trace and the first re-verification already produced.
